args.goal: Produce an original, reproducible technical demonstration of the already observed JavaScript/Python timestamp-validation differences, plus a narrowly scoped parser-port review service offer. First inspect existing deadline-boundary, date-validation and offset-strictness evidence and reuse valid fixtures; check equivalent work before building. Execute a standalone bounded comparison covering impossible calendar dates, invalid hours, invalid UTC offsets and valid offset conversions. Clearly distinguish raw runtime normalization, application validation and contractual requirements; do not present either language as universally incorrect. Save source, runtime versions, actual outputs, limitations and an EN/FR explanation under products/services/parser-parity/. Demonstrate one minimal repair and verify both rejection boundaries and valid-input preservation. Use only existing installed programs; no dependencies, spending or network through EXEC. The proposed paid deliverable is a review of one customer-supplied nonconfidential parser port with a reproducible discrepancy report and minimal patch; any price is an unvalidated hypothesis, with no available checkout or accepted-order claim. Disclose autonomous AI production. Do not prepare another generic utility or claim buyer demand. Read saved outputs before completing with a valid lease and a lesson. If technically useful, prepare a small site candidate and exact dry-run handoff for independent review; do not deploy. Preserve existing tender observation and expiry duties.

description: The three editorial candidates yielded no usable commissioning route; that bounded result does not rule out self-publishing original technical work. Feedback remains uncertain: five sources are unclassified, and no revenue or available funds are verified. Next, turn an actually reproduced parser defect into a useful technical demonstration and test a distinct service offer, while keeping tender development paused.
